IKEBUKURO TOKYO

The Mordell-Weil Lattice of a Rational Elliptic Surface

Dedicated to Professor H. Hironaka on his 60th birthday

by

Keiji OGUISO and Tetsuji SHIODA

(Received January 12, 1991)

## 1. The main result

Let \(S\) be a rational elliptic surface defined over a field \(k\), which is algebraically closed and of arbitrary characteristic. Namely \(S\) is a smooth projective rational surface, with a relatively minimal elliptic fibration \(f : S \to \mathbf{P}^1\), all defined over \(k\). We always assume that \(f\) admits a section \(O : \mathbf{P}^1 \to S\).

Let \(E\) denote the generic fibre of \(f\), which is an elliptic curve over the rational function field \(K = k(\mathbf{P}^1)\). Let \(E(K)\) be the Mordell-Weil group of \(K\)-rational points of \(E\), with the origin \(O\). It is naturally identified with the group of sections of \(f\).

In this paper, we describe the complete structure theorem of the Mordell-Weil group as well as lattice of any rational elliptic surface, in terms of the reducible singular fibres of \(f\).

## 10. Rational elliptic surfaces

In this section, we apply the preceding results to the case where S is a rational elliptic surface with a section. Namely we suppose that S is a (smooth projective) rational surface over k with a relatively minimal elliptic fibration f : S→C, having a global section O : C→S. Then we have C = P¹ (the projective line) and K = k(P¹) = k(t) is a rational function field. We note that the assumption (ii) of (1.1) that f be non-smooth is automatically satisfied in this case. As usual, E/K is the generic fibre.

We recall the well-known results on such a surface S. For the convenience of the reader, we outline the proof assuming the general theory of algebraic surfaces.
